newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM demand boosted by U.S, Euro-growth.
newsitem.headline: DSM demand boosted by U.S, Euro-growth.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV said on Tuesday increased demand prompted by an upturn in European and U.S. economic growth had boosted first-quarter ordinary profits.
"The improvement (in results) is due to the continued good demand and the expansion of our activities," DSM chairman Simon de Bree said in an earnings statement.
The company reported first-quarter ordinary net profit up seven million guilders year-on-year at 223 million.
DSM said that economic growth in Europe had increased slightly in the first 1997 quarter.
In the United States the economy grew faster than expected while growth in Asia remained at a high level, it said.
Net sales were 15 percent up year-on-year at 3.0 billion guilders, reflecting an increase in volumes and selling prices.
"Selling prices, in particular for hydrocarbons, plastics, acrylonitrile and fine chemicals, were higher (up five percent)," DSM said.

Sales volumes rose by seven percent, with higher volume growth for plastics, fertilizers and melamine particularly accounting for three percentage points of the rise. Four percent was due to acquisitions, it said.
Exchange rate movements had a postive effect of three percent on sales, DSM said.
